title: Lazur vs VoiceInk on Mac: screen-aware voice assistant or local dictation app in 2026
metaTitle: Lazur vs VoiceInk on Mac: Price, Privacy and Features
description: Lazur vs VoiceInk on Mac: VoiceInk is a one-time-license dictation app. Lazur is a voice assistant that sees your screen. Compare price, privacy and features.
intro: Lazur and VoiceInk both take your voice on a Mac, but they do different jobs. VoiceInk is a dictation app. It types what you say into the app in front of you, and it transcribes on your Mac by default. Lazur is a voice assistant that sees your screen, answers out loud and dictates too. Pick based on the job you need done, not on the longest feature list.
tldr: VoiceInk is a one-time purchase: Solo $25 for one Mac, Personal $39 for up to two, Extended $49 for up to three.
Lazur is a subscription. Pro is $18 a month, or $15 a month billed annually.
Pick VoiceInk if you mainly dictate and want transcription to stay on your Mac by default.
Pick Lazur if you want voice help that sees your screen, points at controls and runs everyday voice actions.
Neither app runs on Windows today. Lazur lists Windows as planned, and VoiceInk's site mentions no Windows version.

blocks.text: Pricing: a one-time license or a monthly plan

VoiceInk sells licenses, not a subscription. Its pricing page lists three tiers. Solo is $25 for one Mac. Personal is $39 for up to two Macs. Extended is $49 for up to three Macs. Each tier says no monthly bill, and the license covers current and future updates.

Lazur is a subscription. Pro costs $18 a month, or $15 a month when billed annually, and includes 250 AI actions. Power costs $120 a month, or $96 a month billed annually, with 1,000 AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both plans. You can start the 3-day Pro trial without a credit card.

Here is a simple case. You dictate emails and notes on one Mac, and you never ask an app for help with its controls. Solo costs $25 once. Pro costs $18 a month, or $15 a month on the annual plan. The subscription passes the one-time price within two months, even on the annual plan. That comparison only holds if you do not need the extra features. Lazur's price covers voice help with your screen and everyday voice actions, and dictation is included.

items: Comparing $25 with $18 and stopping there. The $18 is per month, so compare over the months you plan to keep the app.
Buying Solo for two Macs. Solo covers one Mac. Personal covers up to two.
Skipping the trial terms. Lazur states its 3-day Pro trial. VoiceInk's pricing page has a free trial button but does not state a length, so read the page before you download.
Forgetting the 14-day money-back guarantee. VoiceInk lists one, so test the app on real work during that window.

blocks.text: Privacy: where your voice and screen go

This is where the two apps differ most. VoiceInk says all transcription happens on your device by default, using local AI models. Its privacy policy says cloud use is opt-in. If you turn it on, audio goes to the transcription provider you pick. Only transcribed text goes to an AI enhancement provider.

Lazur answers questions, so it looks at your screen. It listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so Lazur can answer. They are not stored. Lazur says content is never used to train AI models. Your memory of past requests stays on the Mac.

Retention is different too. VoiceInk keeps transcriptions until you delete them, by default. Its audio cleanup is optional, and the default is 7 days if you turn it on. Read both policies before you decide. The question is which data leaves your Mac and when, not which app sounds more private.

blocks.title: Check cloud settings after install
blocks.text: A third-party review reports cloud transcription settings turning on unexpectedly. That review comes from getvoibe, a competing product, and the report is unattributed. Open VoiceInk's settings and check that each cloud option is off before you dictate anything sensitive.
Dictation: how each app types for you

Both apps type into the app you have open. VoiceInk lists dictation in any app, including email and AI chat. Lazur uses hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor, in any app. Lazur also keeps snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots.

VoiceInk puts more weight on text cleanup. Its homepage lists a custom dictionary, Smart Replace, filler-word and repetition cleanup, and formatting long notes into lists and emails. It can also rewrite selected text from spoken instructions. Lazur's feature list does not mention those, so do not assume Lazur does them.

Here is a quick test. Dictate a status update with three points and one name that is hard to spell. Check the result in your app. Then add the name to the personal dictionary in Lazur or the custom dictionary in VoiceInk, and dictate again. The second pass shows you how each tool handles your own words.

items: Holding the key with no text field selected. Click into a text box first, then hold the key.
Reading the cleanup features as a promise. Check each homepage's feature list before you pay.
Dictating a long draft and sending it unread. In one study, speech left more uncorrected errors in the final text, so scan the result.

blocks.text: Help that sees your screen

Lazur's main difference is that it looks at what is on your screen. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask about anything you see. Lazur answers out loud. Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

Try it on an app you rarely open. Say you need the export option in a PDF editor and cannot find it. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where export is. Lazur circles the control and labels it. You click it. Then ask for the next step, and Lazur waits for your click before it moves on.

Lazur does not do the clicking for you. It does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps. It is not a plugin or add-in for any app. Some people like keeping their hands on every click. Others want the app to do the clicks, and Lazur is not that tool.

VoiceInk's homepage does not describe help like this. Its feature list covers dictation, cleanup, custom vocabulary and rewriting selected text. If your question is where a button is, the features VoiceInk lists do not answer it.
Everyday tasks and background research

Lazur also runs everyday actions by voice. Those include timers, Apple Reminders, Calendar events, notes, music and volume, opening apps and links, web search and Shortcuts. You can set a timer without leaving the document you are writing.

Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs, through the Lazur for Chrome extension. The job comes back with a summary and a report. You can keep working in the meantime, because the research runs in the background.

VoiceInk's feature list does not include timers, reminders, calendar events or web research. For dictation alone, you do not need them. If you want one voice tool for small daily tasks, that gap is the main reason to choose Lazur.

items: Hold ⌥ ⌘ over a screen you do not know and ask where one control is.
Dictate a short email with a name in it, then check the spelling.
Ask for a timer, then check that it goes off when it should.
Run one web research job on a topic you know well, and check the report against what you already know.

blocks.text: Speed: voice input compared with typing

A 2016 study from Stanford and collaborators compared speech and keyboard entry on touchscreen phones. English speech ran at 153 words per minute. Keyboard entry ran at 52. That is 2.93 times faster for speech, on short messages.

The same study found more uncorrected errors in the final speech text. The rate was 1.30% for speech and 0.79% for keyboard. The study tested phones and short messages, not VoiceInk, not Lazur, and not long documents. Treat its numbers as a rough guide, not a verdict on either app.
Platforms and Mac hardware

VoiceInk runs only on Apple silicon Macs. It requires macOS 14.4 or later, and its homepage recommends 8GB of RAM. Its App Store listing is for iPhone and iPad. The Mac app comes from the VoiceInk website.
Lazur runs on macOS with Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available. If your Mac has an Intel chip, VoiceInk does not run on it. Lazur does.

blocks.title: Check your chip and macOS version
blocks.text: Choose Apple menu > About This Mac. An Apple silicon Mac shows a Chip line with an M-series name. VoiceInk needs macOS 14.4 or later, and the same window shows your macOS version.
Three people, three different choices

Take a writer who drafts all day in Pages and Mail. The writer dictates long paragraphs and uses names that autocorrect keeps changing. This person rarely asks for help with a control. VoiceInk fits. Solo at $25 covers one Mac, and the custom dictionary handles the names.

Now take a support lead who works in five apps at once and asks, many times a day, where a setting sits. This person also wants reminders and a timer. Lazur fits better. Hold ⌥ ⌘ to find the setting, and the reminders run through the same tool.

Last, take someone with an Intel MacBook who wants voice help. VoiceInk does not run on that Mac. Lazur supports Intel Macs, so the choice is simple. Try Lazur's trial on real work before you pay for anything.
What to do next

items: Check your chip and macOS version under Apple menu > About This Mac.
If you only need dictation, open the VoiceInk pricing page and read the trial terms there.
If you want help that sees your screen, get Lazur from the [download page](/download) and start the 3-day Pro trial.
Test with one real task from your week, not a demo sentence.
Decide after the test. Keep VoiceInk's 14-day money-back guarantee in mind if you buy it.

blocks.title: Start the trial when you need it
blocks.text: Lazur's trial starts when you first open the app. Install it on a day you have real work to try, not on a quiet weekend.
For more on VoiceInk's design and local dictation, read our [VoiceInk guide](/blog/voiceink-open-source-dictation). For Lazur's plans and limits, see the [pricing page](/pricing).

faq.question: Is Lazur a replacement for VoiceInk?
faq.answer: Only if your main need is dictation. VoiceInk is built to type your voice into any app, with cleanup and formatting. Lazur dictates too, but it also answers questions about your screen and runs everyday voice actions.

faq.question: Does VoiceInk run on Intel Macs?
faq.answer: No. VoiceInk's pricing page says it works only on Apple silicon Macs and requires macOS 14.4 or later. Check your chip under Apple menu > About This Mac.

faq.question: Does Lazur run on Intel Macs?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur runs on macOS with Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available yet.

faq.question: Does VoiceInk send my voice to the cloud?
faq.answer: By default, no. VoiceInk's privacy policy says transcription runs on your device with local AI models. Cloud use is opt-in, and audio goes only to the transcription provider you choose when you enable it.

faq.question: Does Lazur store my audio or screenshots?
faq.answer: Lazur says audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you, and they are not stored. It listens and looks only while you hold the shortcut. Content is never used to train AI models, according to Lazur.

faq.question: How much does VoiceInk cost?
faq.answer: Solo is $25 for one Mac. Personal is $39 for up to two Macs. Extended is $49 for up to three Macs. Each is a one-time purchase with no monthly bill, according to VoiceInk's pricing page.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It draws a circle around a control and guides you one click at a time, waiting for you to click.

faq.question: Does VoiceInk have a free trial?
faq.answer: Its pricing page has a Download Free Trial button, but it does not state a trial length or terms. Read the page before you download. Lazur offers a 3-day Pro trial, and no credit card is needed.

verdict: Pick VoiceInk if most of your voice work is dictation. It fits if you want transcription to stay on your Mac by default and you prefer one payment to a monthly bill. Pick Lazur if you want a voice assistant that sees your screen, points at controls and runs everyday actions. It also dictates. If your Mac has an Intel chip, only Lazur runs on it.
